## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the force-kill ordering fix and the redundant `--stop-recording` resync both work as described. On the force-kill path the indicator refresh now runs after `pkill -9` and the error notification, and a redundant `--stop-recording` requests a refresh before `exit 1`, so a stale "active" icon recovers on the next click. Each of the four new assertions fails when its matching hunk is removed and passes at the PR head. The existing 26 assertions still pass.

One side effect remains on the normal (graceful) stop path.

### Normal stop now keeps the indicator "active" through post-processing

The single refresh moved to the end of `stop_screenrecording()`, after both branches. When the recorder exits within the 5 s grace period, the bar keeps showing the recording icon ("Stop recording") until `finalize_recording` (ffprobe and the ffmpeg trim, loudnorm or libx264 re-encode), the preview thumbnail and the "saved" notification have all finished. The base refreshed as soon as the recorder was gone.

Event order on a graceful stop, from a stubbed run of the real script with the finalize `ffmpeg` call simulated as a 1.5 s step:

```text
                       base          PR head       per-branch (suggested)
recorder seen gone     t=0           t=0           t=0
indicator refresh      +0.002 s      +1.528 s      +0.007 s
                       (before       (last event,  (before
                        finalize)     after notify) finalize)
```

**Impact:** the icon is misleading, with no data loss. How long it stays wrong depends on how long post-processing takes. Timing the head's own finalize commands on synthetic 1080p60 media on a fast 16-CPU host gave about 1.3 s per recorded minute with audio (loudnorm) and about 8 s per recorded minute on the libx264 re-encode path. Slower machines, like the throttled laptop that motivated this PR, will take longer. A click during that window still recovers because of this PR's redundant-stop refresh. History: `aabaef83` moved the refresh ahead of post-processing, and this PR restores the earlier end-of-function placement.

**Suggested change:** refresh inside each branch, so the force-kill path keeps the new ordering and the graceful path refreshes before post-processing. This variant passes the PR's test file unchanged.

```bash
  if pgrep -f "^gpu-screen-recorder" >/dev/null; then
    pkill -9 -f "^gpu-screen-recorder"
    omarchy-notification-send -u critical -t 5000 "Screen recording error" "Recording process had to be force-killed. Video may be corrupted."
    toggle_screenrecording_indicator
  else
    toggle_screenrecording_indicator
    finalize_recording
    ...
```

**Optional test improvement:** the new tests do not exercise the graceful stop path, so the head's end-of-function placement passes them. An assertion that the refresh precedes the finalize `ffmpeg` call would catch this, using a `pgrep` stub that reports the recorder alive for the first calls and gone afterwards, plus logging `ffprobe`/`ffmpeg` stubs.

**Optional:** SIGKILL delivery is asynchronous, and the new ordering test only checks that `pkill -9` was invoked first (its `pgrep` stub stays "alive" throughout). A recorder stuck in uninterruptible I/O could in principle still be visible to the indicator probe right after `pkill -9`. This was not reproduced, and the redundant-stop refresh now recovers it on the next click. A short bounded wait until `pgrep` stops matching would remove the dependency. The original indicator code had a 0.2 s wait for the same reason.

**Description note:** #9296 is still open and unmerged, so "the QML watchdog fixed in #9296" overstates its status. The redundant-stop resync also relies on the QML status probe finishing, because `refresh()` in `ScreenRecording.qml` returns early while `statusProc` is running. A stuck probe remains that PR's scope.
